questions.question: In the passage, the word "liquidity" most nearly means
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

Financial markets often appear intimidating because they contain specialised terms that describe different investment strategies and risks. However, many of these concepts can be understood through simple examples. Consider a trader who believes that the price of wheat will rise three months from now. Instead of purchasing wheat immediately, the trader enters into a derivative contract - an agreement whose value depends on the future price of an underlying asset. In simple terms, it is a promise-based deal linked to what might happen in the future.

Markets also depend heavily on liquidity, which refers to how easily an asset can be bought or sold without causing a significant change in its price. Cash is considered highly liquid because it can be used immediately, while certain rare assets may take longer to sell. High liquidity generally makes markets more efficient and attractive to investors.

Some investors seek to reduce risk through hedging. A farmer, for example, may use a derivative contract to lock in a future selling price for crops, protecting against unexpected price declines. In contrast, hedge funds often employ a wide range of sophisticated strategies to generate returns. These strategies may include short selling, where an investor borrows an asset and sells it with the expectation of buying it back later at a lower price.

Another commonly discussed concept is leverage. Leverage involves using borrowed money to increase the size of an investment. While this can magnify profits when prices move favourably, it can also amplify losses if the market moves in the opposite direction. For this reason, financial experts frequently emphasise that higher potential rewards are often accompanied by higher risks.

options.label: B
options.text: The ease with which an asset can be bought or sold

options.label: C
options.text: A contract linked to future prices

options.label: D
options.text: Money borrowed from a financial institution

questions.solution:
Among the given options, (b) is the correct answer because the passage defines liquidity as "how easily an asset can be bought or sold without causing a significant change in its price." Thus, liquidity refers to the ease with which an asset can be converted into cash or traded in the market. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

Option (a) is incorrect because liquidity is not the same as profit.

Option (c) is incorrect because it describes a derivative contract rather than liquidity.

Option (d) is incorrect because borrowed money relates to leverage, not liquidity.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.solution:
Option (c) has been spelt incorrectly. The correct spelling is 'neither' which means not one of two. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

'Obedient' means willing to comply with commands.

'Martyr' means one who sacrifices one's life.

'Harass' means to annoy someone frequently.

questions.question: In the passage, the word "foundation" most nearly means
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the questions:

Few nutrients receive as much attention today as protein. Fitness influencers promote high-protein diets, food manufacturers advertise protein-enriched products, and many consumers carefully track their daily intake. As a result, protein has become one of the most discussed macronutrients of the modern era. Yet, despite this widespread interest, the scientific understanding of protein is relatively recent.

The word "protein" did not exist until 1838, when the Dutch chemist Gerardus Mulder isolated protein as a distinct molecular substance and studied its role in living organisms. The term was derived from a Greek word meaning "of primary importance," reflecting the belief that protein was fundamental to life. Mulder's work helped establish protein as a key component of biological tissues and laid the foundation for later advances in nutritional science.

Proteins perform numerous functions within the body. They contribute to the structure of muscles, skin, organs, enzymes, and hormones. However, modern discussions often focus narrowly on muscle growth and the quantity of protein consumed. Some nutrition experts argue that this emphasis can overlook a more important consideration: tissue quality. Building healthy, functional tissue depends not only on consuming sufficient protein but also on factors such as overall diet, physical activity, sleep, and metabolic health.

Consequently, many researchers suggest that the conversation should move beyond simply asking how much protein people consume. A more meaningful question may be whether that protein supports the development and maintenance of healthy tissues. In this sense, tissue quality may be more important than tissue quantity alone.
questions.solution:
Among the given options, (c) 'basis' is the correct answer because the passage states that Mulder's work "laid the foundation for later advances in nutritional science." In this context, "foundation" refers to the underlying basis or groundwork upon which future developments are built. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

Option (a) "origin" refers to the point of beginning but does not accurately capture the idea of supporting later developments.

Option (b) "obstacle" is incorrect because it means something that hinders progress.

Option (d) "limitation" refers to a restriction and does not fit the context.

questions.source: SSC CGL Tier II Live Test: Oct 9-11
questions.question:
Choose the sentence that uses a homonym of the underlined word.

The actor took a final bow after the performance.

options.label: A
options.text: The audience applauded as he took a bow.

options.label: B
options.text: She tied a decorative bow around the gift box.

options.label: C
options.text: The dancer ended the show with a graceful bow.

options.label: D
options.text: Everyone stood up during his final bow.

questions.solution:
In the question, bow refers to bending the body as a gesture of respect.

In option (b), bow refers to a ribbon tied into loops.

Options (a), (c), and (d) use bow in the same sense as the question.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.source: SSC CGL Tier II Live Test: Oct 23-25
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There needs to be better ______ between departments to improve workflow.
questions.solution:
The correct option to fill in the blank is "communication."

'Communication' in the given context refers to the exchange of information, ideas, or messages between departments. Improved communication is essential for coordinating efforts, resolving issues, and streamlining workflow.

Other words do not fit the context:

'Combat' implies conflict or fighting, which is opposite of the desired outcome.

'Aviation' refers to air travel or the aircraft industry, which is unrelated to interdepartmental workflow.

'Canister' refers to a container for storing or transporting goods, which has no relevance to workflow or departmental interactions.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: There needs to be better communication between departments to improve workflow.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Elaborate
questions.solution:
The word 'elaborate' is an adjective meaning involving many carefully arranged parts or details; detailed and complicated in design and planning. The most apt antonym of the given word is 'minimal' (of a minimum amount, quantity, or degree; negligible). Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Complicated - Consisting of many interconnecting parts or elements; intricate.

Detailed - Having many details or facts; showing attention to detail.

Addicted - Physically and mentally dependent on a particular substance.

questions.source: SSC CGL Tier II Live Test: Oct 16-18
questions.question:
Fill in the blank.

A strong feeling of _____ filled Ron's heart after winning the race.
questions.solution:
The blank requires a noun to be filled with, since it is preceded by the preposition 'of'.

'Great' is an adjective, so it is eliminated.

'Sabotage' is a verb, so it is eliminated.

'Contentment' is the noun that grammatically and contextually fits in the blank, conveying that Ron's heart was satisfied after winning the race.

Therefore, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Choose the correct antonym of "VILIFY":
questions.solution:
To "Vilify" means to speak ill of or defame.

"Praise" is the correct antonym as it means to commend or express approval.

"Denigrate", "Malign", and "Defame" are synonyms sharing the same negative meaning.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Every cloud has a silver lining

options.label: A
options.text: Bad things one day eventually lead to good things

options.label: B
options.text: Stuck in a difficult circumstance with no escape

questions.solution:
'Every cloud has a silver lining' means bad things one day eventually lead to good things or even the worst things have some positive side. So, the correct option is option a).

· The figurative expression for 'stuck in a difficult circumstance with no escape' is - back against the wall.

· The figurative expression for 'eating too excessively' is - eat like a horse.

· The figurative expression for 'being ignored' is - left out in cold.

questions.question:
Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank.

Elephants are used in some countries for ______ timber.
questions.solution:
Let's look at the meanings of the given options.

Howling: producing a long, doleful cry or wailing sound.

Hauling: pull or drag with effort or force.

Holing: make a hole or holes in.

Halling: an acrobatic Norwegian dance in duple measure for one to three single dancers.

After observing the meanings of each option, we can say that 'hauling' is the most appropriate choice.

The correct sentence is: Elephants are used in some countries for hauling timber.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.source: SSC CGL Tier II Live Test: Oct 23-25
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Other questions were designed to obtain information about the extent of its use as ______ by the respondent.
questions.solution:
The sentence tells that certain questions were framed in order to extract/retrieve information about a particular thing, so 'perceived' is the apt choice for the given blank so as to convey that the required information is the perception of the respondents. The rest of the words are incorrect because these do not form a meaningful sentence when placed in the blank.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question:
Choose the word from the options that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Anarchy
questions.solution: 'Anarchy' means 'A state of disorder due to absence or non-recognition of authority or other controlling systems'. Options c) and d) can be rejected as they are unrelated to the word. 'Lawlessness' means 'A state of disorder due to a disregard of the law'. Hence, option a) can also be rejected as it has the same meaning as the word. 'Fastidious' means 'Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail'. 'Recuperate' means 'Recover from illness or exertion'. Hence, option b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The artist created a surreal landscape that seemed to defy the laws of physics and reality.
questions.solution:
"Surreal" means having qualities that are strange or dream-like, often defying normal reality and expectations.

Realistic: Representing things as they are in real life; practical.

Imaginary: Existing only in the imagination; not real.

Subtle: Not obvious; delicate or understated.

Serene: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled.

The most appropriate synonym from the given options is "imaginary," as it denotes something that exists in the realm of imagination rather than reality. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Her paltry knowledge of the subject became evident during the discussion.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate antonym for "paltry" is 'substantial'.

"Paltry" describes something as insignificant, trifling, or very small in amount or degree.

"Substantial" means significant, considerable, or ample in amount, size, or importance.

Curtate: Short.

Precise: Exact, accurate, or carefully prepared.

Meagre: Lacking in quantity or quality; insufficient.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate homophones to fill in the blanks.

She withdrew her ___________ from the ___________ when he agreed to pay off the debt.
questions.solution:
Option (a) is the correct choice.

A sale is the exchange of a commodity for money or the action of selling something. A sail is a sailing ship. The sentence is about a person who withdrew from selling her ship.

Complete sentence: She withdrew her sail from the sale when he agreed to pay off the debt.

questions.question: The word "illumination" most nearly means:
questions.passage:
Directions : Read the passage and answer the following questions:

The development of rechargeable emergency bulbs has transformed the way households manage power interruptions and energy efficiency. In earlier times, sudden electricity failures often left homes dependent on candles, kerosene lamps, or battery-powered torches, which provided only temporary and limited illumination. The introduction of rechargeable LED bulbs offered a more reliable solution by combining regular lighting with automatic emergency backup systems.

These bulbs function through an inbuilt rechargeable battery that stores electrical energy during normal power supply. While connected to electricity, the bulb simultaneously provides illumination and charges its internal battery. During a power outage, the stored energy automatically powers the bulb, enabling it to continue emitting light without requiring manual switching or additional equipment. This dual functionality has made rechargeable bulbs particularly useful in regions experiencing frequent electricity disruptions.

Modern rechargeable bulbs employ Light Emitting Diode (LED) technology, which consumes significantly less energy while producing brighter and longer-lasting illumination. Many advanced models also incorporate features such as portable hooks, multiple brightness settings, and rapid charging mechanisms, increasing their convenience and adaptability. These innovations have reduced dependence on traditional emergency lighting devices and contributed to more sustainable household energy consumption.

From simple backup lighting systems to intelligent energy-efficient devices, rechargeable bulbs represent a practical convergence of convenience, sustainability, and technological advancement - an increasingly essential feature of modern living.
questions.solution:
Solution:

The passage uses the word "illumination" in the context of lighting systems and the production of light. Therefore, the word refers to brightness or the act of providing light. Among the given options, "Radiance" is the closest in meaning because it denotes brightness or glowing light. "Fragility" refers to weakness or delicacy, which is unrelated to lighting. "Obscurity" means darkness or lack of clarity, which is opposite in meaning to illumination. "Saturation" refers to complete absorption or intensity, especially of colour or liquid, and does not convey the idea of light itself. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution:
"Seperate" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "separate", which means to cause to move or be apart.

"Supersede" is correctly spelt. It means to take the place of (a person or thing previously in authority or use); supplant.

"Tommorrow" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "tomorrow", which refers to the day after today.

"Unforseen" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "unforeseen", which means not anticipated or predicted.

The only correctly spelt word among the options is "supersede".

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word.

The scientist was praised for her ___ methodology, which left no room for bias or error.
questions.solution: 'Scrupulous' means meticulous, extremely careful, making it the correct choice. Other options are incorrect spellings. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To drink from the poisoned well

options.label: A
options.text: To engage in morally questionable acts

options.label: B
options.text: To suffer from accepting dangerous or corrupt influence

questions.solution:
This idiom refers to accepting something that appears beneficial but is dangerous or harmful.

Example: "He drank from the poisoned well when he allied with the corrupt officials."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Zealot
questions.solution:
King- the male ruler of an independent state, especially one who inherits the position by right of birth.

Soldier- a person who serves in an army.

Fanatic- a person filled with excessive and single-minded zeal, especially for an extreme religious or political cause.

Visitor- a person visiting someone or somewhere, especially socially or as a tourist.

The meaning of the word 'zealot' is 'a person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuit of their religious, political, or other ideals'. Among the given options, the word that matches the meaning of the given word is option (c), 'fanatic'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Play a blinder

options.label: A
options.text: To perform with a lot of skill.

options.label: D
options.text: To choose to ignore behaviour that you know is wrong.

questions.solution: The idiom 'play a blinder' means to perform with a lot of skill, especially when you are playing sport. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A place where dead bodies are kept
questions.solution:
A morgue is a facility where dead bodies are temporarily stored, typically for identification, autopsy, or investigation, especially in cases of unnatural or suspicious deaths.

A cemetery is a designated area where the dead are buried.

A vault is a large room or chamber used for storage, especially an underground one. While it can house bodies, it is not as commonly used as a temporary storage place for bodies before burial or cremation like a morgue or mortuary.

A crematorium is a facility where dead bodies are cremated (burned to ashes).

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: What is the exact one-word name for a long thrusting spear historically used by infantry soldiers fighting in tight formation?
questions.solution:
Option (a) is correct because a PIKE is specifically a very long spear used by foot soldiers in formation. The rule-based clue is "long thrusting spear" plus "infantry soldiers"; both together eliminate weapons mainly meant for throwing or cavalry use.

• Option (b) JAVELIN is designed primarily for throwing, not for sustained close-formation thrusting.

• Option (c) HALBERD is a pole weapon with an axe-blade and spike, not simply a long thrusting spear.

• Option (d) LANCE is chiefly associated with mounted warriors rather than infantry ranks.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Indifferent to pain and pleasure
questions.solution:
WORDMEANING
Pessimistictending to see the worst aspect of things or believing that the worst will happen.
Stoica person who can endure pain or hardship without showing their feelings or complaining.
Secludednot seen or visited by many people; sheltered and private.
Soliloquya speech in a play which the character speaks to himself or herself.

So, 'stoic' is the right word here.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question: Select the correct Synonym of "SLANDER".
questions.solution:
The word "Slander" means a false spoken statement damaging to someone's reputation.

1) "Calumniate" - correct synonym; to make false and defamatory statements.

2) "Laud" - opposite; to praise.

3) "Revere" - opposite; to deeply respect.

4) "Adulate" - unrelated; to flatter excessively.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.
